executive_summary: A fleet worker that finishes an SD and holds no active claim ends its turn via the Stop hook's wind-down/park path without ever re-checking the belt for claim-ready work -- directed assignments and self-claimable drafts then sit queued until the worker's NEXT check-in tick. A measured specimen showed three finisher seats idle for ~40 minutes beside two claim-ready drafts until the coordinator manually dispatched. This SD adds a SAME-TURN next-claim attempt to the Stop hook's ALLOW-PATH (scripts/hooks/stop-loop-wakeup-reminder.cjs): when a worker-shaped session ends its turn holding no claim, it makes exactly one call into the existing canonical checkin resolution path (worker-checkin.cjs's resolveCheckin) before parking, and if that call resolves a claim, blocks the stop and instructs the worker to continue building it immediately instead of going idle. Verified by 26 new unit tests including two regressions that catch a real defect found during review (an allowlist classifier that silently dropped two live, unconditionally-reachable claim-acquiring ladder rungs).

functional_requirements.title: Same-turn next-claim attempt on the wind-down ALLOW-PATH
functional_requirements.description: In scripts/hooks/stop-loop-wakeup-reminder.cjs's main(), inside the existing `if (workerShaped)` ALLOW-PATH branch (the branch that already computes workerShaped and was about to call parkSessionRecoverable + recordWindDown), attempt ONE same-turn next-claim before parking: query for claim-ready work via the SAME canonical resolution ladder every worker /checkin uses (worker-checkin.cjs's resolveCheckin), and either continue building the claimed work (via a Stop-hook decision:'block') or fall through to the pre-existing park path unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: The wind-down path provably attempts a next claim same-turn when workerShaped && !hasActiveClaim
No claim predicate, guard, or priority rule is duplicated -- resolveCheckin is called, not re-implemented

functional_requirements.title: Never attempt a second claim while one is already held
functional_requirements.description: shouldAttemptSameTurnClaim({hasActiveClaim, workerShaped}) returns true ONLY when workerShaped is true AND hasActiveClaim is false. A worker still holding an SD claim (mid-work, or armed-with-claim ending its turn) must never be diverted into this path -- it must finish or hand off its current claim per the existing wind-down handshake, never grab a second one.

functional_requirements.title: Honor all existing claim guards and directed-assignment priority
functional_requirements.description: Because the attempt delegates to resolveCheckin (the exact function scripts/worker-checkin.cjs's own /checkin CLI uses), every existing guard is inherited automatically: sweep-claim safety, peer/foreign-claimant guards, tier gates, canary fence, quota locks, and directed-assignment-before-self-claim priority. No new predicate is introduced that could diverge from the canonical ladder.
acceptance_criteria: A queued directed assignment plus a claim-ready draft: resolveCheckin's own internal step order resolves the directed assignment first; the caller (attemptSameTurnNextClaim) makes exactly one call and does not separately attempt self-claim

functional_requirements.title: Correct claim-outcome classification (denylist, not allowlist)
functional_requirements.description: attemptSameTurnNextClaim classifies resolveCheckin's returned .action using a DENYLIST of non-claim terminal actions (idle, idle_fable_propose, error) -- anything else is treated as a real claim. This was corrected during review from an initial ALLOWLIST design that silently misclassified two live, unconditionally-reachable claim-acquiring ladder rungs (resume_final from recover-stranded-final.cjs, and resume_orphan from adopt-orphan.cjs -- neither gates on ctx.mySd) as none-claimable, which would have let a session take a real claim and then immediately park itself as idle, manufacturing a fresh orphan while the log line reported the opposite of what happened.
acceptance_criteria: resolveCheckin returning action:'resume_final' or action:'resume_orphan' is classified outcome:'claimed'
A hypothetical future ladder action not yet denylisted is claimed-by-default, never silently dropped
Regression tests exist proving the original allowlist defect would have been caught (mutation-tested: reverting to the allowlist fails exactly 3 targeted tests)

functional_requirements.title: Bounded, single-attempt, fail-open, budget-aware
functional_requirements.description: The attempt is bounded by a timeoutMs derived from the hook's existing work-budget tracking (remainingBudgetMs() - TELEMETRY_RESERVE_MS). A timeout, a timeoutMs<=0 (budget exhausted), a throwing resolution, or an idle/error resolution are all treated identically as 'none-claimable', falling through to the unchanged existing park+recordWindDown path. No polling loop or busy-wait is introduced -- exactly one attempt per wind-down.
acceptance_criteria: timeoutMs<=0 skips the resolveCheckin call entirely (never invoked)
A slow resolution past timeoutMs reports none-claimable, not an error or a hang
A throwing resolveCheckinFn reports none-claimable, never propagates

functional_requirements.title: Single log line + dashboard-observable metadata stamp
functional_requirements.description: Every wind-down traversal of the workerShaped branch emits exactly one stderr log line: '[same-turn-next-claim] claimed:<key>' or '[same-turn-next-claim] none-claimable'. The same outcome is best-effort merged into claude_sessions.metadata.same_turn_claim_attempt={outcome, key, at} (mirroring the existing recordWindDown read-modify-merge pattern), making 'chose to exit after looking' distinguishable from 'never looked' on the same dashboard record.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one stderr line matching /\[same-turn-next-claim\]/ per allow-path traversal (source-pinned test)
recordSameTurnClaimAttempt fails open on a DB error without throwing

technical_requirements.title: Single-file source change
technical_requirements.description: Only scripts/hooks/stop-loop-wakeup-reminder.cjs is modified. worker-checkin.cjs is read-only, consumed via its existing resolveCheckin export -- no changes to the claim ladder itself (explicit non-goal).

technical_requirements.title: Independent kill switch
technical_requirements.description: LEO_SAME_TURN_NEXT_CLAIM env var (default 'on') gates the new behavior independently of the pre-existing LEO_LOOP_WAKEUP_REMINDER enforcement flag and its own enforcementDisabled kill switch -- these are different concerns (dispatch efficiency vs. wakeup-arm enforcement) and must be rollback-able independently.

technical_requirements.title: No schema or migration changes
technical_requirements.description: Pure application-code addition to an existing Stop hook plus a metadata JSON merge on the pre-existing claude_sessions.metadata column; no new tables or columns.

test_scenarios.scenario: Claim-ready fixture present, no active claim, worker-shaped
test_scenarios.expected: attemptSameTurnNextClaim reports outcome:'claimed' via the single resolveCheckinFn call

test_scenarios.scenario: Directed assignment + claim-ready draft both present
test_scenarios.expected: resolveCheckin's own priority resolves the directed assignment; attemptSameTurnNextClaim makes exactly one call and reports that outcome
outcome:'none-claimable', falls through to unchanged park path

test_scenarios.scenario: resume_final / resume_orphan claim actions (regression for the fixed defect)
test_scenarios.expected: Both classified outcome:'claimed', not silently dropped

test_scenarios.scenario: Slow resolution exceeding timeoutMs, or already-exhausted budget (timeoutMs<=0)
test_scenarios.expected: outcome:'none-claimable', resolveCheckinFn never invoked when timeoutMs<=0

acceptance_criteria: The wind-down path provably attempts a next-claim same-turn for a finisher holding no claim
All existing claim guards and directed-assignment priority are honored via delegation to resolveCheckin
Empty-belt wind-down behavior is unchanged except one log line
Every wind-down emits exactly one claimed:<key> or none-claimable line, observable on the claude_sessions dashboard record

risks.risk: Production timeout budget (~2s remaining after existing DB round-trips) may cause resolveCheckin to routinely time out under real load
risks.mitigation: A timeout degrades identically to an empty belt (both report none-claimable and fall through to the unchanged park path) -- fail-open by design, no behavioral divergence, accepted per this SD's own success criterion 3

risks.risk: resolveCheckin performs coordination side-effects (roll-call registration, message acks) beyond a pure claim query, now running on the wind-down path
risks.mitigation: Accepted tradeoff: reusing the canonical, already-guarded checkin ladder is lower-risk than forking a parallel claim-only query that could drift from the guards it must honor (explicit non-goal: do not touch claim predicates)

consumers: Every fleet worker session running under /loop that ends a turn via the Stop hook
dependencies: The pre-existing shouldParkRecoverable/workerShaped computation already present in the hook
data_contracts: claude_sessions.metadata gains an additional same_turn_claim_attempt key (additive, non-breaking)
runtime_config: LEO_SAME_TURN_NEXT_CLAIM=off disables the new behavior without a redeploy, falling back to the pre-existing park-only path
observability_rollout: [same-turn-next-claim] stderr log line on every wind-down traversal; claude_sessions.metadata.same_turn_claim_attempt for dashboard/fleet-wide aggregation

system_architecture.summary: Four new functions added to the existing Stop hook, wired into its pre-existing ALLOW-PATH branch; no new files, no new services.

components.name: scripts/hooks/stop-loop-wakeup-reminder.cjs
components.change: adds isSameTurnClaimEnabled, shouldAttemptSameTurnClaim, attemptSameTurnNextClaim, recordSameTurnClaimAttempt, and wires them into main()'s existing workerShaped ALLOW-PATH branch

implementation_approach.summary: Additive functions plus a single call-site insertion ahead of the pre-existing park logic, reusing the canonical claim-resolution path rather than duplicating it.
steps: Add the kill-switch and pure predicate function
Add the bounded, fail-open attempt function delegating to resolveCheckin
Add the best-effort dashboard-observability metadata stamp function
Wire all three into main()'s existing workerShaped branch, ahead of parkSessionRecoverable
Fix the classifier to a denylist after VALIDATION caught an allowlist gap that dropped two live claim-acquiring actions

All 143 hook tests pass (no regression to the pre-existing 117 tests in the same directory)
